entries.name: The Forum of Aeterna
entries.summary: Aeterna's civic square, where law, market and religion share one pavement.
entries.body:
Every Invictian city is laid out around a forum: a paved, colonnaded square with the basilica on one side, the chief temple on another and the speakers' platform between them. Proclamations are read here, elections are canvassed here, and the price of bread is argued about here in public. It is the Roman forum, and an Invictian abroad navigates by it.

## In Aeterna

Aeterna's forum is the original that every other is copied from, and it is too small for the city it serves: hemmed in by seven centuries of temples and basilicas, crowded from dawn, and the place where [[The Annona]]'s grain shortfalls are first felt in the form of a crowd.

entries.name: The Baths of Aeterna
entries.summary: Aeterna's public baths, where the city does its bathing, its gossip and most of its business.
entries.body:
Invictian baths are civic, cheap and nearly universal: a sequence of cold, warm and hot rooms over a furnace-heated floor, an exercise yard, and benches enough for a city's business to be conducted in them. Most citizens bathe daily. Most deals are made wet.

## In Aeterna

The great baths of the capital are free or nearly so, and they are where Aeterna actually lives. Business, gossip and politics happen here rather than in the tenements, which have no room for any of them.

entries.name: The Basilica of Aeterna
entries.summary: Aeterna's hall of law: courts, contracts and the property registers under one roof.
entries.body:
The basilica is an Invictian city's hall of law: a long roofed hall with an apse at the far end where the magistrate sits. Cases are heard, contracts witnessed and property registered under one roof and in public, on the principle that law done privately is not law.

## In Aeterna

The capital's basilicas hear cases from across the Imperium. Their registers are where the city's bankers first noticed the coin was being debased, before the [[Temple of Juno]] said so at the quarterly assay.

entries.name: The Aeterna Garrison
entries.summary: The legion's camp at Aeterna, kept outside the sacred line as Invictian law requires.
entries.body:
Invictian law keeps soldiers outside a city's sacred boundary, so the garrison stands beyond the walls: a rectangular fortress on the standard plan, a gate on each side, the headquarters at the crossing of the two main streets. Since the Treaty of Deiperdeum, who these camps answer to has become the Imperium's central question.

## In Aeterna

No legion may camp inside the sacred line, so Aeterna's soldiers sit beyond it: [[The Obsidian Phalanx]] in its ancient quarters, the Legates' retinues in the suburbs, and thousands of unpaid veterans with nowhere to go. Inside the walls the only armed body is [[The Vigiles]].

Romulo's basilica keeps the guild charters, the Imperium's founding documents, in its vaults. They are read aloud in full once a year to a thin audience.

The legionary fortress stands two miles out, not in the city, and its Legate has been building a personal following among his veterans. The city council has noticed and can do nothing about it.

entries.name: The Agora of Hellarchon
entries.summary: Hellarchon's agora: market, assembly ground and the place anyone may speak.
entries.body:
Every Hellenorian city has its agora: an open square framed by stoas, where the market trades in the mornings, the courts sit in the colonnades, and the citizen body meets to argue. It is the Greek agora exactly, and its rule is the League's: anyone may speak, and everyone will answer.

## In Hellarchon

Hellarchon's agora sits on the upper city's rock, beneath the acropolis. Here the assembly that commands the League's fleet meets and votes, and here the other cities' envoys wait to be heard.

entries.name: The Temple Precinct of Hellarchon
entries.summary: The walled sacred ground of Hellarchon, home of its patron's temple and its dedications.
entries.body:
A Hellenorian sanctuary is a walled sacred ground, a temenos, around the city's chief temple: altar outside, cult image within, and every open space crowded with dedications from citizens who want the god and their neighbours to know what they gave. Each city keeps its own patron and its own version of the story.

## In Hellarchon

The great sanctuary crowns the acropolis, white stone visible a day out at sea. The Greater Panegyris ends here each year after its procession up from the harbour.

entries.name: The Gymnasion of Hellarchon
entries.summary: Hellarchon's gymnasion: exercise ground, school and the citizens' club.
entries.body:
The gymnasion is exercise ground, school and club at once: a running track, a wrestling floor, and colonnaded rooms where teachers lecture and old men talk politics. It is where Hellenorian boys become citizens, and where the League's philosophers find their audiences.

## In Hellarchon

Hellarchon's gymnasia feed the [[Arcane Academy]] as much as the athletic games: the city's young magi train their bodies and their arguments in the same colonnades.

entries.name: The Theatre of Hellarchon
entries.summary: Hellarchon's open-air theatre, cut into the hillside for festival drama and the assembly.
entries.body:
A Hellenorian theatre is cut into a hillside: a curve of stone seats above a circular dancing floor and a stage building behind it. Plays are performed only at festivals, in competition, before the whole citizen body. Between festivals the assembly often meets here, which is why so many plays are about politics.

## In Hellarchon

The theatre of the Dionysia, where for four days a year plays criticise the powerful with a licence that does not extend to the rest of the calendar.

entries.summary: Corinth's agora: market, assembly ground and the place anyone may speak.

## In Corinth

Corinth's agora is the busiest and least decorous in the League, crowded with shippers, toll-farmers and every people on the continent. Corinthian tolerance is a business decision.

The port's temples are unusually well-endowed and unusually busy. They cater to sailors, which is to say they run on the money of men who may not come back.

Corinth's gymnasion trains the athletes of the Isthmian Games, the League's second-greatest, held here every two years under a truce that even tyrants observe.

The theatre is new money's favourite gift to the city. Corinth's rich sponsor its festivals lavishly, and are looked down on by older cities for it.

The gymnasion is where the city's citizen phalanx is made. Thebesieas drills to a standard the maritime cities cannot match, and the sacred band trains here.

Thebesieas built its theatre late and reluctantly. It is used more for the reading of the sacred band's roll than for plays.

Thessalonika's agora is the tidiest in the League: a planned square on the city grid, its stoas glazed against the northern cold.

The sanctuary stands in the upper town among the academies. Its priests bless the harbour on the day the first ice appears in the fountains.

Thessalonika's gymnasia are as much academies as exercise grounds. Their porticoes host the Disputation, where scholars argue positions assigned by lot.

## In Thessalonika

The theatre holds the Reading, where new works are read aloud and heckled before publication. Several careers have ended on its stage.

entries.name: The Bazaar of Persemenid
entries.summary: Persemenid's roofed market streets, each trade with its own lane, gate and warden.
entries.body:
An Acheaorian bazaar is a district, not a square: roofed lanes laid out by trade, coppersmiths in one, spice-sellers in another, each lane with its own gate, its own warden and its own guild. Prices are bargained, never posted, and bargaining is a social ritual that a stranger is expected to fail at.

## In Persemenid

Persemenid's bazaar lies in the ordinary city below the platform, among the mud-brick houses and water channels, and supplies the court above.

entries.name: The Fire-Temple of Persemenid
entries.summary: The house of Persemenid's sacred flame, kept by the Magi and never allowed to die.
entries.body:
Every Acheaorian city of any size keeps a fire-temple, the Persian atashkadeh: a heavy, plain building around an inner chamber where the Magi tend a flame that must never go out. The public may see the fire through a screen but not approach it. The Magi's calendar, set by the tending of the fire, governs the working year.

## In Persemenid

Persemenid's great fire-temples stand on the hilltop chain from which the Magi mark the Fire Watch, signalling from temple to temple across the plateau.

entries.name: The Caravanserai of Persemenid
entries.summary: The great walled inn at Persemenid where caravans stable, sleep and trade.
entries.body:
A caravanserai is a walled courtyard inn built for caravans: stabling and storerooms on the ground floor, lodging above, one fortified gate that is shut at night. Every road into an Acheaorian city ends at one, and each becomes a small foreign quarter of whoever travels that road.

## In Persemenid

The royal caravanserai receives the satrapies' delegations before the Bringing, when each climbs the stair in the order the relief shows them.

entries.name: The Water-Court of Persemenid
entries.summary: Where [[The Qanat Network]] surfaces at Persemenid and the city's water shares are measured out.
entries.body:
Acheaorian cities live on water brought underground from distant hills by [[The Qanat Network]]. Where the channel surfaces there is a water-court: a cool vaulted chamber where the flow is divided into shares, each measured by a timed bowl and owned by deed. The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold most of the shares, which is why the guild is quietly one of the powers in every Acheaorian city.

## In Persemenid

Below the platform, Persemenid's water-court feeds both the city and the gardens of [[The Paradise of Persemenid]].

entries.name: The Bazaar of Atarabad
entries.summary: Atarabad's roofed market streets, each trade with its own lane, gate and warden.
entries.body:
An Acheaorian bazaar is a district, not a square: roofed lanes laid out by trade, coppersmiths in one, spice-sellers in another, each lane with its own gate, its own warden and its own guild. Prices are bargained, never posted, and bargaining is a social ritual that a stranger is expected to fail at.

## In Atarabad

The commercial capital of [[Acheaoria]] has the largest bazaar on the continent. During the Long Bargain, prices here are fixed by public negotiation rather than in private.

entries.name: The Fire-Temple of Atarabad
entries.summary: The house of Atarabad's sacred flame, kept by the Magi and never allowed to die.

## In Atarabad

Atarabad is oriented on its fire-temple, a squat, heavy building on the highest ground, where the Magi hold that the flame has never been extinguished.

entries.name: The Caravanserai of Atarabad
entries.summary: The great walled inn at Atarabad where caravans stable, sleep and trade.
entries.body:
A caravanserai is a walled courtyard inn built for caravans: stabling and storerooms on the ground floor, lodging above, one fortified gate that is shut at night. Every road into an Acheaorian city ends at one, and each becomes a small foreign quarter of whoever travels that road.

## In Atarabad

Atarabad has one caravanserai for each major road, each a small foreign quarter of its own. On the Opening of the Roads they all send their first convoy out on the same morning.

entries.body:
Acheaorian cities live on water brought underground from distant hills by [[The Qanat Network]]. Where the channel surfaces there is a water-court: a cool vaulted chamber where the flow is divided into shares, each measured by a timed bowl and owned by deed. The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold most of the shares, which is why the guild is quietly one of the powers in every Acheaorian city.

## In Atarabad

The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold Atarabad's water shares, which makes the guild one of the city's powers despite having no seat on anything.

entries.name: The Bazaar of Mithratal
entries.summary: Mithratal's roofed market streets, each trade with its own lane, gate and warden.
entries.body:
An Acheaorian bazaar is a district, not a square: roofed lanes laid out by trade, coppersmiths in one, spice-sellers in another, each lane with its own gate, its own warden and its own guild. Prices are bargained, never posted, and bargaining is a social ritual that a stranger is expected to fail at.

## In Mithratal

Mithratal's bazaar is quiet for its size, like the rest of the city. Its busiest stalls sell writing materials and seals.

entries.name: The Fire-Temple of Mithratal
entries.summary: The house of Mithratal's sacred flame, kept by the Magi and never allowed to die.
entries.body:
Every Acheaorian city of any size keeps a fire-temple, the Persian atashkadeh: a heavy, plain building around an inner chamber where the Magi tend a flame that must never go out. The public may see the fire through a screen but not approach it. The Magi's calendar, set by the tending of the fire, governs the working year.

## In Mithratal

Mithratal's fire burns before the oath precinct, and the Magi witness every covenant sworn there.

entries.name: The Caravanserai of Mithratal
entries.summary: The great walled inn at Mithratal where caravans stable, sleep and trade.
entries.body:
A caravanserai is a walled courtyard inn built for caravans: stabling and storerooms on the ground floor, lodging above, one fortified gate that is shut at night. Every road into an Acheaorian city ends at one, and each becomes a small foreign quarter of whoever travels that road.

## In Mithratal

The waiting lodges for parties to a covenant began as caravanserais and are still built like them: walled, with one gate.

entries.name: The Water-Court of Mithratal
entries.summary: Where [[The Qanat Network]] surfaces at Mithratal and the city's water shares are measured out.
entries.body:
Acheaorian cities live on water brought underground from distant hills by [[The Qanat Network]]. Where the channel surfaces there is a water-court: a cool vaulted chamber where the flow is divided into shares, each measured by a timed bowl and owned by deed. The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold most of the shares, which is why the guild is quietly one of the powers in every Acheaorian city.

## In Mithratal

Mithratal's water shares are themselves covenants, registered and read out with the rest at the annual Renewal.

entries.name: The Bazaar of Persevalis
entries.summary: Persevalis's roofed market streets, each trade with its own lane, gate and warden.
entries.body:
An Acheaorian bazaar is a district, not a square: roofed lanes laid out by trade, coppersmiths in one, spice-sellers in another, each lane with its own gate, its own warden and its own guild. Prices are bargained, never posted, and bargaining is a social ritual that a stranger is expected to fail at.

## In Persevalis

Persevalis's bazaar is mostly fruit, cuttings and seed, sold under the trees of the public orchards.

entries.name: The Fire-Temple of Persevalis
entries.summary: The house of Persevalis's sacred flame, kept by the Magi and never allowed to die.
entries.body:
Every Acheaorian city of any size keeps a fire-temple, the Persian atashkadeh: a heavy, plain building around an inner chamber where the Magi tend a flame that must never go out. The public may see the fire through a screen but not approach it. The Magi's calendar, set by the tending of the fire, governs the working year.

## In Persevalis

The fire-temple stands at the top of the terraces, where the water enters the city, and the Magi bless the Opening of the Channels each spring.

entries.name: The Caravanserai of Persevalis
entries.summary: The great walled inn at Persevalis where caravans stable, sleep and trade.
entries.body:
A caravanserai is a walled courtyard inn built for caravans: stabling and storerooms on the ground floor, lodging above, one fortified gate that is shut at night. Every road into an Acheaorian city ends at one, and each becomes a small foreign quarter of whoever travels that road.

## In Persevalis

The caravanserai sits at the foot of the slope, where the green ends and the plateau's ordinary dust begins.

entries.name: The Water-Court of Persevalis
entries.summary: Where [[The Qanat Network]] surfaces at Persevalis and the city's water shares are measured out.
entries.body:
Acheaorian cities live on water brought underground from distant hills by [[The Qanat Network]]. Where the channel surfaces there is a water-court: a cool vaulted chamber where the flow is divided into shares, each measured by a timed bowl and owned by deed. The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold most of the shares, which is why the guild is quietly one of the powers in every Acheaorian city.

## In Persevalis

Persevalis is the water-court made into a city. Water runs along every terrace, and the right to each channel is written into the deed of the house it passes.

entries.name: The Bazaar of Xerastri
entries.summary: Xerastri's roofed market streets, each trade with its own lane, gate and warden.
entries.body:
An Acheaorian bazaar is a district, not a square: roofed lanes laid out by trade, coppersmiths in one, spice-sellers in another, each lane with its own gate, its own warden and its own guild. Prices are bargained, never posted, and bargaining is a social ritual that a stranger is expected to fail at.

## In Xerastri

Xerastri's bazaar lies between the two walls, in the ward that everyone understands would be given up in a serious assault.

entries.name: The Fire-Temple of Xerastri
entries.summary: The house of Xerastri's sacred flame, kept by the Magi and never allowed to die.
entries.body:
Every Acheaorian city of any size keeps a fire-temple, the Persian atashkadeh: a heavy, plain building around an inner chamber where the Magi tend a flame that must never go out. The public may see the fire through a screen but not approach it. The Magi's calendar, set by the tending of the fire, governs the working year.

## In Xerastri

The fire-temple stands inside the inner wall with the granaries and wells: the fire is one of the things Xerastri will not give up.

entries.name: The Caravanserai of Xerastri
entries.summary: The great walled inn at Xerastri where caravans stable, sleep and trade.
entries.body:
A caravanserai is a walled courtyard inn built for caravans: stabling and storerooms on the ground floor, lodging above, one fortified gate that is shut at night. Every road into an Acheaorian city ends at one, and each becomes a small foreign quarter of whoever travels that road.

## In Xerastri

During the Horse Fair, steppe clans are let into the outer city to trade at the caravanserai under truce. It is heavily policed and very profitable.

entries.name: The Water-Court of Xerastri
entries.summary: Where [[The Qanat Network]] surfaces at Xerastri and the city's water shares are measured out.
entries.body:
Acheaorian cities live on water brought underground from distant hills by [[The Qanat Network]]. Where the channel surfaces there is a water-court: a cool vaulted chamber where the flow is divided into shares, each measured by a timed bowl and owned by deed. The [[Bountiful Harvesters]] hold most of the shares, which is why the guild is quietly one of the powers in every Acheaorian city.

## In Xerastri

Xerastri's wells are inside the inner wall, and its water-court is kept there too. In a siege, water is the citadel's argument.

entries.name: The Sacred Line of Aeterna
entries.summary: The ancient boundary inside which no soldier may bear arms, which is why Aeterna's legions camp outside it.
entries.body:
The boundary matters more than the walls. Aeterna's sacred line, the Roman pomerium, is marked by low stones and is older than the city it encloses. Inside it no soldier may bear arms, no army may camp, and the only lawfully armed body is [[The Vigiles]].

That single rule has shaped the capital's politics for eight hundred years. It is why [[The Obsidian Phalanx]] is quartered beyond it, why a Legate entering the city lays down his command at the line, and why, five years after the Treaty, everyone is watching to see whether someone steps over it under arms.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Insulae of Aeterna
entries.summary: The capital's tenements: brick blocks six and seven storeys high, where most Aeternans live, cook and burn.
entries.body:
Behind the marble of the public city is the city people actually live in: brick-faced concrete tenements six and seven storeys high, plaster coming off, streets narrow enough that two carts stop each other. Most Aeternans rent rooms above shops, cook on charcoal in rooms that should not have fire in them, and eat out because their homes have no kitchens.

The insulae burn regularly enough that [[The Vigiles]] are the busiest institution in the Imperium. Burial here is by subscription to the [[Cycle of the Eternal Bloom]], for most citizens the most important contract they will ever sign.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Founder's Hut
entries.summary: A humble hut, reverently rebuilt for nine centuries, said to stand where the Imperium was founded.
entries.body:
At the heart of Romulo stands a hut that is certainly not the original, rebuilt in the same form every time it decays, for nine centuries. It is said to mark where the founder of the Imperium lived when the Imperium was a market town with ambitions.

The Founding ends here each year after a full day of processions, and every Invictian magistrate is expected to attend at least once. Invictians come to be reminded that the Imperium was once small.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Old Wall of Romulo
entries.summary: Romulo's ancient wall of mortarless stone, walked each year in procession to re-mark the sacred line.
entries.body:
Romulo is walled in stone laid without mortar, and has not been fortified beyond it since the Imperium grew strong enough that fortifying the founding city would be an insult. Inside it, building above two storeys needs a licence that is essentially never granted.

Once a year the wall is walked in procession and the sacred line re-marked, with the [[Verdant Sentinel Order]] providing the escort.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Eleven Bridges of Mavelon
entries.summary: Mavelon's pride: eleven bridges over a fast river, each kept by a guild that cuts its mark on the parapet.
entries.body:
Mavelon straddles a fast river on eleven bridges, and the bridges are the only thing the city is vain about. Each is older than it looks, and each is maintained by a guild that carves its mark into the parapet.

At the Bridge Walk every bridge is crossed in procession by its guild and the marks are recut. A bridge whose guild fails to appear is a scandal, and in the past has been a revolution.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Mill Banks of Mavelon
entries.summary: Mills and forges along both riverbanks, under a permanent haze: the Imperium's arsenal.
entries.body:
Along both banks of the river run the mills and forges that make Mavelon the Imperium's arsenal: smoke, hammering, and a haze that never lifts off the water. Downstream the river runs discoloured for a mile, which the city regards as evidence of prosperity.

At midwinter, on the Quenching, every forge quenches at the same moment. The guild halls on the banks keep four centuries of apprentices' first pieces.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Great Sanctuary of Ephelanum
entries.summary: The vast temple at the end of Ephelanum's marble street, visible far out to sea, and the city's reason to exist.
entries.body:
At the end of the marble street from the harbour stands a temple large enough to be seen from well out at sea, its colonnade alone a century's work. Like the great temple at Ephesus it is also a bank: it holds deposits under sanctuary protection, lends, and is by some measures the largest single holder of coin in the region.

Each year the goddess's statue is carried from the temple to the harbour and back in the Procession of the Image, a full day with the whole city behind it.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Silting Harbour of Ephelanum
entries.summary: Ephelanum's harbour, dredged four times and losing: the city's quiet crisis.
entries.body:
Ephelanum's harbour is silting up. It has been dredged four times, and the sea is retreating anyway, leaving the waterfront further from the water every generation.

The annual Dredging is nominally a rite for the harbour's health. In practice it is a yearly reminder of the silt, and attendance has been falling.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Relay Station of Aepistra
entries.summary: The Cursus Legionis station at Aepistra, where official riders change horses on the Imperium's roads.
entries.body:
The relay stations of the *Cursus Legionis* run through Aepistra, and its station is one of the busiest in the provinces: stables, a posting house, and a constant traffic of official riders, tax documents and orders, changing horses on the road to and from [[Aeterna City]].

Whoever controls the station sees the province's correspondence first, which is why the Legate's men are always in the posting house.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Shipsheds of Hellarchon
entries.summary: The long roofed sheds where the world's largest fleet is berthed, each one numbered and accounted for.
entries.body:
The harbour below Hellarchon is tar, timber and noise, and its long roofed shipsheds hold the largest fleet in the world. Each shed is numbered and each berth accounted for. The triremes here are the League's common defence in name and Hellarchon's hegemony in fact.

In spring, at the Launching, the fleet is drawn from the sheds and rowed out in formation. It is nominally a rite and unmistakably a demonstration.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Long Walls of Hellarchon
entries.summary: The walls that join Hellarchon's hill city to its harbour two miles below, making one fortress with a port inside it.
entries.body:
Hellarchon was built twice: the old town on its rock and the harbour two miles below. Walls run the whole distance between them, so the two are one fortress with a port inside it, impossible to starve while the fleet holds the sea.

Along the walls is where most of the city's people actually live. Hellarchon's wealth is on the hill and its population is on the road.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: Arcane Academy
entries.summary: Hellarchon's renowned school of magic, which draws ambitious magi from across the planes.
entries.body:
At the heart of [[Hellenoria]] lies Hellarchon, called Aetherion by its people, and at the heart of Hellarchon is the Arcane Academy, which the court scribe [[Selenarion of Helarchon]] describes as a place 'where reality is reshaped by will alone'. It draws ambitious magi from across the planes, eager to unlock the secrets of the cosmos.

The violet skies over the city at dusk are popularly said to come from ancient magic. The official histories footnote the claim to a redacted vault record.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Haulway of Corinth
entries.summary: A paved track across the isthmus on which whole ships are dragged overland between Corinth's two seas.
entries.body:
Between Corinth's two harbours runs a paved haulway with grooves cut for wheeled cradles, on which entire ships are dragged overland from one sea to the other, like the diolkos of ancient Corinth. A cargo that crosses here saves several days and a dangerous cape, and Corinth charges accordingly.

It never stops: ox teams, capstans, and the shriek of a hull winched across stone. The season's first ship across is decorated and crewed by the city's magistrates, who are notoriously bad at it.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Upper Fortress of Corinth
entries.summary: The fortified rock above Corinth, the strongest position in Hellenoria, never taken by assault.
entries.body:
Above the isthmus rises a fortified rock that dominates both harbours. Like the Acrocorinth, it is the strongest position in [[Hellenoria]] and has never been taken by assault.

Corinth has never needed much of an army: it has the rock, a modest fleet, and a great deal of money to hire other people.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Street of Counting-Houses
entries.summary: Corinth's money street, where rival banks keep branches side by side.
entries.body:
After [[Hellarchon City]], Corinth is the League's chief money market, and its bankers keep to one street. The branch offices of the [[Mithril Reserve]] and the [[Vaults of Equilibrium]] sit on it side by side, watching each other.

The [[Luminastra Alchemists]] keep their largest workshop nearby, because every ingredient on the continent passes through Corinth's warehouses.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Sacred Way of Delphara
entries.summary: The switchback road up to Delphara's temple, lined with the treasuries of rival cities.
entries.body:
The road from the valley of olives to Delphara's temple climbs in switchbacks, and the whole ascent is lined with treasuries: small, exquisite buildings raised by individual cities to house their dedications, each competing with its neighbours in stone.

The effect is a road through eight centuries of Hellenorian rivalry, told entirely in architecture, ending at a temple where the god is asked questions.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Oracle of Delphara
entries.summary: The temple at the summit where petitioners pay to put their question to the god.
entries.body:
At the top of the sacred way is the temple of the oracle. Consultation is not free: a petitioner pays for the sacrifice, the attendance and the interpretation, and the fee scales with the question. Delphara produces nothing and is extremely rich, which the [[Scales of Eternal Justice]] have noted in writing.

In the winter months the god is held to be absent. The temple stays shut during the Silence and the town empties.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Solar Precinct of Helionyx
entries.summary: An open court with a gnomon and a graduated arc, read every clear day for six hundred years.
entries.body:
At Helionyx's highest point is the solar precinct: an open court with a gnomon at its centre and a graduated arc cut into the pavement. It has been read and the reading recorded every clear day for six hundred years.

At the summer solstice, the Standing, the exact moment is announced and the whole city falls silent. The year's tables are published at the Reading of the Arc, attended by scholars from three empires.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Dye-Works of Helionyx
entries.summary: The vats on Helionyx's edge, whose season opens each year with the city's least fragrant festival.
entries.body:
On the edge of the white city, downwind, are the dye-works. The season's first vat is opened in public at the Dyeing, a festival whose smell is famously appalling and whose attendance is mandatory for the guild.

The colours made here are worn across the League, and the white city's wealth is, somewhat ironically, in them.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Citadel of Thebesieas
entries.summary: The inland city's fortress, with its own water: built by a city that expects to be attacked by land.
entries.body:
Thebesieas expects to be attacked by land, and its architecture says so: heavy walls, gates that are genuinely gates, and a citadel with its own water supply, so that it can hold out after the lower city falls.

The citadel keeps the roll of the sacred band. At the Naming of the Band, the living answer for the dead.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Porticoes of Thessalonika
entries.summary: The upper town's long colonnades, where teaching is done in public and interrupting is expected.
entries.body:
Thessalonika's upper town is institutions: academies, libraries, guild halls, and the long porticoes where teaching is done in public and interrupting is expected. Courtyards are enclosed and windows glazed, for this is the coldest city in [[Hellenoria]].

The porticoes host the Disputation, five days of public academic contest in which positions are assigned by lot, so a scholar may have to defend the opposite of everything he has written.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Sea Wall of Thessalonika
entries.summary: The long wall along Thessalonika's bay, guarding a waterfront of warehouses.
entries.body:
Thessalonika lies on a curved bay behind a long sea wall, with warehouses along the waterfront and a citadel on the slope above. It is the tidiest large city on the continent, built to a plan it still follows.

The harbour is blessed on the day the first ice appears in the upper town's fountains. The date is recorded, and a late frost is considered an omen.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Royal Stair of Persemenid
entries.summary: The great stair up to Persemenid's platform, wide enough for ten horsemen abreast and lined with the tribute relief.
entries.body:
Persemenid's platform is cut into the rock forty feet above the plain and approached by a stair wide enough for horsemen to ride up ten abreast. It is meant to be climbed slowly. Along it runs a relief of tribute-bearers, every subject people in its own dress carrying what it owes, so a visitor climbs alongside the whole empire bringing gifts, as at Persepolis.

At the Bringing, every satrapy that still acknowledges the throne sends its delegation up the stair in the order the relief shows. Which ones do not come is the year's real news.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Audience Hall of Persemenid
entries.summary: The columned hall on the platform: the largest roofed space on the continent, where the King of Kings receives.
entries.body:
On the platform stands the columned audience hall, the largest roofed space on the continent, modelled on the Apadana. Here the King of Kings receives the satrapies, and here nothing is ordinary and nothing is accidental.

[[The Ten Thousand]] hold the platform. Their first regiment quarters inside the precinct and is drawn from the old nobility, which makes it a guard and a hostage-house at once.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Wind-Tower Quarter of Atarabad
entries.summary: Atarabad's inward-turned houses under roofed streets and wind-towers that pull cool air into the rooms below.
entries.body:
Atarabad is built to exclude the sun: streets roofed with matting, courtyards turned inward, and wind-towers on every roof of consequence pulling cool air down into the rooms below. The great houses of the merchant city sit here, each with its own armed guard.

The [[Gilded Vault]] and the [[Wheelwalkers]] both keep their headquarters in this quarter. The gems and bullion moving through it have grown alarming in volume as the satrapies turn restless.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Precinct of Oaths
entries.summary: The open stone court at Mithratal's centre, where oaths are sworn and every road ends.
entries.body:
Mithratal is arranged so that every road runs to the place where oaths are sworn: an open precinct, roofless, floored in one expanse of dressed stone and empty of decoration. It is named for Mithra, god of the covenant and the binding word.

A new slab is laid in the floor each decade, cut by the [[Geolith Artisan Covenant]]. Once a year, on the Silent Day, nothing said in the city is binding, and people say what they think.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Covenant Archives of Mithratal
entries.summary: Where every covenant sworn in Mithratal is drafted, registered and read out at the annual Renewal.
entries.body:
Mithratal's wealth went into the buildings around the precinct: the archives where covenants are kept, the chambers where terms are drafted, and the lodging where parties wait out the required intervals.

At the Renewal every standing covenant registered in the city is read out by class, and any party wishing to dispute one must do so then or hold its peace for another year.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Terraced Gardens of Persevalis
entries.summary: The terraces that make Persevalis a hillside of trees with roofs showing through.
entries.body:
Persevalis is terraced down a long slope, with water led along every level, so that it is a series of gardens with buildings in them rather than the reverse. Every house of consequence has a walled garden with a channel through it, and the public spaces are orchards. This is the Persian paradise garden on the scale of a city.

On the Night Gardens of high summer, lamps are lit in every walled garden, the gates are left open, and the city walks through each other's houses until dawn.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Outer Wall of Xerastri
entries.summary: The taller of Xerastri's two walls, facing the Malaunian Steppe.
entries.body:
Xerastri is two walls and a ditch with the city between them. The outer wall faces the [[Malaunian Steppe]] and is the taller. Every stretch of it belongs to a family responsible for its upkeep, and at the Counting of the Wall each spring the families formally report on their sections.

Once a year the garrison rides out in full muster in view of the steppe. Everyone on both sides understands the message.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Inner Citadel of Xerastri
entries.summary: The older inner wall enclosing Xerastri's citadel, granaries and wells: what the city keeps if it loses everything else.
entries.body:
The inner wall is the older and encloses the citadel, the granaries and the wells. The space between the walls is where most people live, and everyone understands that in a serious assault that space is expendable.

The empire's best siege engineers are stationed here, with nothing to besiege, and keep the engines in order anyway.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Treaty Hall of Deiperduem
entries.summary: The plain hall where the Treaty of Deiperdeum was signed, preserved exactly as it was on the day.
entries.body:
On the square of the old town stands the Treaty Hall: unglamorous, deliberately plain, and preserved exactly as it was on the day the three empires signed. Its plainness is the point. No empire could be seen to have built it.

At the Signing each year all three empires send delegations, the document is displayed, and every speech is checked in advance by everyone. At dusk comes the Quiet Hour, when the war dead are read out as three figures with no names. It is the only occasion on which nobody argues.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Embassy Compounds of Deiperduem
entries.summary: Walled embassy quarters, each with its own colours and guards, each pretending not to watch the others.
entries.body:
In five years Deiperduem has rebuilt itself into embassies: walled compounds, each flying its own colours, each with its own guard, each pretending the others are not watching. The Treaty forbids any empire to station troops in the city, so the guards are described as household staff.

The town council counts them, publishes the count and complains, and the numbers rise anyway. Order outside the walls is kept by the city watch and the [[Ironclad Legion]] under contract.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Old Town of Deiperduem
entries.summary: The small, unremarkable old town at Deiperduem's centre: now the most expensive ground on the continent.
entries.body:
The old town in the middle of Deiperduem is small, unremarkable, and now the most expensive property on the continent. Its notaries, translators and copyists are the best available and price accordingly.

In high summer the Market of Nations fills it, each empire's goods in its own quarter. It is nominally a trade fair and in practice the year's most productive week of unofficial negotiation.
entries.sourcePath: authored: scripts/build-city-locations.ts (landmark from the city's own write-up)

entries.name: The Molten Crucible
entries.summary: An upscale alchemist and artificer in the Noble Districts, run jointly by the Vulkrim and Virellarion families.
entries.body:
An upscale alchemist's and artificer's in the Noble Districts of the [[Duneforged Citadel]], managed by two noble houses at once: [[The Vulkrim Family, Marquis]] and [[The Virellarion Family, Count]].

Each house runs its own shop lower down the Citadel: the Virellarions' [[The Gilded Crucible]] in alchemy and the Vulkrims' [[Ember & Anvil]] in smithing. The Molten Crucible is where the two trades, and the two families, meet: enchanted metalwork and alchemical craft for the Citadel's upper streets.

entries.name: The Temples
entries.summary: The temples kept within the Citadel Cathedral of Duneforged, one for each patron the Citadel honours.
entries.body:
The [[Citadel Cathedral]] of the [[Duneforged Citadel]] keeps a temple for each of the powers the Citadel honours, Titans and Invictian gods alike:

- [[Forge of Vulcan]], for Vulcan, the Artisan of Creation
- [[Temple of Juno]], for Juno, the Protector of Bonds, where the coin is assayed
- [[Vault of Mercury]], for Mercury, the Trickster of Trade
- [[Shrine of Anchiale]], for the Titan of fire and craft
- [[Sanctum of Hoplodamus]], for the Titan of Guardianship, patron of the trials at [[The Ju Colliseum]]

That Titans are honoured beside the Imperium's gods is a Duneforged peculiarity. Elsewhere the Titans' worship is older and stranger than any state cult.
